featured_reviews.name: Indranil Bhattacharjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
JSW Centre, located in the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) of Mumbai, serves as the corporate headquarters for JSW Group, one of India's leading conglomerates with interests spanning steel, energy, infrastructure, cement, and more.

Architectural Highlights
The JSW Centre is recognized as one of Mumbai's largest open office complexes. Its architectural design features two elliptical structures that merge seamlessly, reflecting a blend of modern aesthetics and functionality. The building incorporates advanced sustainable technologies and contemporary office configurations.

From below the building looks like a ship. There is a well maintained cafeteria/canteen at the first floor (also called atrium floor). I had Espresso coffee there and I can confidently say it was great. The aroma, the taste, everything was awesome. The food at the Canteen is also delicious. There is a central hollow space around which the offices are built.

Overall the office complex is very well maintained, well furnished, neat and clean. The toilets are of International standard and very clean.

Strategic Location
Situated in the heart of Mumbai's financial district, the Bandra Kurla Complex, JSW Centre benefits from excellent connectivity and proximity to major business hubs.

The only con I noticed was that there was no place for visitors to sit in front of the building or even at the reception at the ground floor. So unless you are at the reception in the Atrium floor there is no where you can sit. This is really inconvenient and inconsiderate.

featured_reviews.name: pranali chirme
featured_reviews.review_text:
♥️🍴
I recently dined at Kokan Tadka, a restaurant that specializes in Kokani and Goan-style cuisine, and it was an unforgettable experience. This place is a treasure trove of authentic regional flavors that truly impress.

The variety of thalis offered here is exceptional. I tried both the chicken and mutton thalis, and each was a feast in itself. The chicken thali featured tender, well-spiced chicken curry, accompanied by a variety of sides that perfectly complemented the main dish. The mutton thali was equally delightful, with succulent pieces of mutton cooked to perfection in a rich, flavorful gravy.

One of the standout dishes for me was the crispy javla bhaji. The crispy texture and unique flavor of the javla (small, dried fish) paired wonderfully with the bhaji, making it a must-try for anyone looking to explore authentic Kokani cuisine.

To round out the meal, Kokan Tadka serves a variety of Maharashtrian bhakris. These traditional flatbreads, made from different grains, are the perfect accompaniment to the rich and spicy curries.

Overall, Kokan Tadka is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience the true taste of Kokani and Goan cuisine. The diverse thali options, delicious crispy javla bhaji,and authentic Maharashtrian bhakris make it a culinary destination worth exploring. Don't miss out on this gem if you're in the area!

GIA India Laboratory Private Limited is widely recognized as one of the most trusted and authoritative diamond and gemstone grading laboratories in the country. As part of the globally respected Gemological Institute of America, the laboratory operates with the highest standards of accuracy, independence, and integrity, reinforcing confidence in diamonds and gemstones across the Indian and international markets.

One of the strongest qualities of GIA India Laboratory Private Limited is its unwavering commitment to scientific precision. Every diamond and gemstone is examined using advanced technology and strict grading methodologies that are consistent with global GIA standards. This ensures reliable, unbiased, and internationally accepted grading reports, which are highly valued by manufacturers, traders, retailers, and consumers alike.

The laboratory is known for its highly skilled team of gemologists and technicians who undergo rigorous training and continuous skill development. Their expertise, combined with standardized procedures, ensures consistency and transparency in every report issued. This professionalism plays a crucial role in maintaining trust and credibility throughout the gems and jewelry supply chain.

GIA India Laboratory Private Limited also stands out for its state-of-the-art facilities. Equipped with advanced instruments and modern testing systems, the laboratory is capable of handling high volumes while maintaining exceptional accuracy and quality control. Its efficient processes and adherence to strict timelines make it a reliable partner for businesses in the diamond and gemstone industry.

Another important strength of the laboratory is its ethical approach. GIA’s strict policies on independence and objectivity ensure that grading results are free from commercial influence. This ethical framework helps protect the integrity of the trade and supports fair practices across the industry.

Overall, GIA India Laboratory Private Limited represents excellence, trust, and global consistency in diamond and gemstone grading. Its scientific rigor, professional expertise, advanced infrastructure, and ethical standards make it a cornerstone of reliability in the Indian gems and jewelry industry.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Barbeque Nation (BKC) on Friday for a birthday celebration with my cousins, and honestly, the experience was very disappointing.

The overall management felt completely off. Only a few starters were served, and something as basic as crispy corn was a total letdown. The main course, as expected, lacked taste. At the counters, there were no spoons or plates available, and even after informing the staff, nothing was managed properly.

Service was equally frustrating. The person at the chaat counter kept disappearing every 5–10 minutes. Even after we complained, instead of fixing the issue, the same person started managing the falooda counter as well—leaving both counters unattended at times. It genuinely felt like there was no interest in serving customers properly.

The falooda and ice cream section was another letdown. There was no one to guide or explain what varieties were available. For someone visiting for the first time, it’s impossible to know what to try without any assistance.

Seating was also uncomfortable. We were 4 adults and a child, yet were made to sit at a 4-seater table. Even after requesting a better arrangement, we were told no tables were available.

The staff assigned to our table seemed overburdened, constantly running between multiple tables. While it’s understandable, it clearly reflects poor staffing and mismanagement.

What made it worse was that this was a pre-informed birthday celebration. At the end, they just handed over the cake—no effort, no celebration, no basic gesture like clapping or music. It completely spoiled the mood.

Overall, it felt like a very poorly managed experience and a big drop in standards. Sadly, I won’t be visiting again.

featured_reviews.name: dhara rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Barbecue Nation at BKC expecting a pleasant dining experience, but unfortunately, it turned out to be extremely disappointing.
Before visiting, we searched for Barbecue Nation on Google and received a call from the call center. We were informed by Mr. Mohit about a special offer where the final difference after discount would be only around ₹150, inclusive of taxes.
Upon reaching the restaurant, we were excited to enjoy the vegetarian buffet. However, the experience started badly when the barbecue starters served at our table were extremely spicy, with a chilli flavour so overpowering that it was literally hurting our throats. We informed the staff, and the skewers were replaced, but the quality and taste remained unsatisfactory.
Things got worse when we visited the salad counter. The pasta salad was clearly stale and had a foul smell. We immediately informed the staff and requested that it be removed from the counter. We also tried the sev puri from the chaat section, but it was completely flat and tasteless, consisting of little more than puri, chutney, and sev.
To their credit, the chef personally came to our table and tried to address our concerns. He prepared fresh items for us and even acknowledged that the food quality was not up to the expected standard. However, by then our dining experience had already been ruined.
We requested the staff to simply provide the bill as we no longer wished to continue with the meal. To make matters worse, the billing did not match the offer that had been communicated to us. We were told the price would be ₹849 per person inclusive of taxes, but the bill was generated at ₹899 per person plus GST. We had to call the call center again and spend nearly 20 minutes arguing about the offer they themselves had provided. Instead of enjoying our meal, we were left dealing with unnecessary stress and confusion.
Despite all the inconvenience, poor food quality, misleading offer communication, and wasted time, we paid the full bill.
The hygiene standards were also unacceptable. The washrooms were dirty, dustbins were overflowing, and the entire area was wet and poorly maintained.
Overall, this was one of the worst dining experiences we have had. The food quality, hygiene, customer service coordination, and billing transparency were all far below expectations. The experience was certainly not worth the amount paid. If possible, I would give negative marks for this visit.

featured_reviews.name: Arzan Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
BKC DIVE is one of those places you mostly hear about because of its buffet pricing. Pocket-friendly, filling, and popular — which explains why it’s almost always crowded. We went knowing exactly that, and the experience more or less matched expectations, with a few highs and a few misses.

The atmosphere is lively and energetic. It’s busy, noisy, and constantly moving, but not in a bad way. You can feel the buzz the moment you walk in, mainly because people are here to eat well without burning a hole in their wallet. For a buffet place in BKC, it does a decent job of handling the crowd, though peak hours can feel a bit packed.

Coming to the food, we opted for the buffet. The starters were honestly the best part of the meal. Fresh, flavourful, and regularly refilled — these are the dishes you actually enjoy going back for. The desserts were also surprisingly good for a buffet setup, offering a sweet and satisfying end to the meal.

The main course, however, was where things dipped a little. Nothing was bad, but nothing really stood out either. Most dishes felt just okay — edible, filling, but missing that extra flavour or excitement. You eat it, you’re satisfied, but you don’t feel the urge to go back for seconds.

Service was a bit inconsistent. The staff was polite, but we did have to request the same dishes multiple times, which gets slightly frustrating when you’re hungry and the place isn’t exactly empty. Given how crowded it gets, it’s understandable to an extent, but smoother coordination would definitely improve the experience.

Overall, BKC DIVE is a decent buffet spot if your priority is value for money. It’s not a place you go to be impressed by gourmet flavours, but if you want a relaxed, budget-friendly meal with good starters and desserts, it does the job. Go with the right expectations, and you’ll leave reasonably happy.

featured_reviews.name: Nandita Mundle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I walked into BKC Dive on a Saturday evening (21st Feb) with a friend hoping to have a drink and some appetizers. What i got was a plate of the worst customer service i have seen - and this is just at the door. The man who takes your name and seats you ("the host") asked me for my Name & phone number. I gave my name and - when I said I don't want to give my phone number, he was unsure what to do but took down my request for Table for 2.

Dive had many empty tables. But he asked us to wait at the bar till he finds us a table. This is normal in most pubs so we walked over to the bar. However unlike other pubs, BKC Dive has no bar stools or chairs at the bar. So we came back to stand near the door next to the Host who was supposed to give us a table. On the way we did see empty tables for 2.

We came back and mentioned to him that there are tables available (there was no one else waiting). What followed was the most bizarre conversation I have had:

Me: I think there a couple of empty tables for 2 near the bar.
The Host man: You give me your phone number, then I can give table.
Me: Do you mean if I don't give you my phone number we don't get a table?
The Host Man: Then, when you go outside to smoke, you need to leave your ID card here. (Wutt?!)
Me: I don't want to go outside. I have just come in. I want to sit down and have a drink. I don't smoke either. Why do you need my ID?
The Host Man: <no reply>

At this point we chose to leave rather than continue that ridiculous conversation.

I understand restaurants like to do data collection for marketing - but refusing service since we didn't pander to their data collection is the most bizarre experience I have ever seen.

Definitely would not visit that place again.

featured_reviews.review_text: I loved both the dishes we had. Nice place to eat and drink

The food was average – not bad, but not something I’d go back specifically for. Drinks menu is decent, and they have happy hours which is a plus. Service was a bit slow, and the staff seemed distracted at times.

Overall, it’s an okay spot for a casual evening if you’re in the area, but don’t expect anything too great.
